title: Protocol and Cover
premise: Zephyrine Sterling, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call he couldn't save, is summoned when Flight 447's passenger manifest, radar trace, and booking records evaporate mid-flight — yet the plane lands and its passengers walk out claiming nothing is wrong. Investigating off-book, he discovers the flight carried a witness to a government-sanctioned massacre, and that erasing the record was step one of erasing everyone aboard. To survive until dawn, Zephyrine must trade his own buried secret — the identity of the man who really caused his failed negotiation three years ago — to a rogue intelligence officer who controls the border checkpoint where the last witnesses are trapped. He gives up the truth he's protected for years, buys the survivors their escape, and walks away cleared but hollow, learning that justice outside the law always bills someone.
about_author: Isandro Coldharbour is the pen name of a former crisis-line coordinator who spent six years listening to the worst nights of strangers' lives before turning them into fiction. He writes from a coastal town he refuses to name, where the fog rolls in on schedule and the records stay intact.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine. Three years after losing hostage Marisol Vance on a botched negotiation, Zephyrine works by-the-book cases and tutors rookies, teaching them rules he no longer believes. A late-night call pulls him to a regional airport: Flight 447 has landed, but every digital trace of it has vanished. The emotional beat is restless dread — a man who trusts procedure watching procedure fail.

chapters.title: Passengers Without Shadows
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine. The deplaned passengers check into hotels, smile at cameras, and insist they flew nowhere; their luggage tags are blank. One woman, Ilse Brandt, slips Zephyrine a matchbook with coordinates inside before security escorts her away. The beat is creeping wrongness: the horror isn't violence, it's consensus — everyone agreeing on a lie.

chapters.title: What the Manifest Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine. Following the coordinates, Zephyrine finds a burned safehouse and a surviving manifest fragment listing one name twice: a whistleblower named Tomas Reyes who witnessed the Kestrel Valley massacre. An old contact warns him the deletion order came from inside the ministry. Beat: cold clarity — this is cover-up, not glitch, and he's already on the list.

chapters.title: Rules Are a Kind of Cage
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Zephyrine and Major Adaeze Okonkwo, the intelligence officer running the erasure. Okonkwo believes wiping the flight prevents a war; she studies Zephyrine's file and finds his buried secret about the Vance failure. Beat: two professionals recognizing each other across a widening moral gap — both think they're protecting people.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes at Gate Nine
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine. Okonkwo offers him a deal: walk away and keep his secret, or lose everything. Instead Zephyrine negotiates — the skill that ruined him — buying twelve hours by promising to deliver Reyes himself. Beat: the seduction of the deal, and the old shame stirring as he realizes he's negotiating with a state instead of a gunman.

chapters.title: Ilse in the Interstice
chapters.summary: POV: Ilse Brandt. Hiding in airport maintenance tunnels, Ilse reveals she was the flight attendant who smuggled Reyes's evidence off the plane in pieces distributed among passengers' belongings. She's dying of a pre-existing condition and wants the truth out more than survival. Beat: fragile alliance and borrowed courage from someone with less to lose.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint Shifts at Dawn
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine. The survivors are being funneled toward the border checkpoint, where the night shift — the only officers not yet compromised — rotates out at 6 a.m. Zephyrine maps the timing: anyone still inside when the shift changes disappears like the flight did. Beat: ticking-clock pressure and the geometry of an impossible choice.

chapters.title: Everything Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine. Cornered by Okonkwo's team, Zephyrine plays his only card: proof of who actually gave the fatal order during the Vance negotiation — his former mentor, now a ministry director. He offers it as leverage. Beat: the terrible intimacy of betrayal, sacrificing a dead man's reputation to buy living strangers a chance.

chapters.title: Six O'Clock Somewhere
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Zephyrine and Okonkwo. At the checkpoint, Zephyrine stalls the corrupt shift commander while Ilse moves the survivors through; Okonkwo, holding Zephyrine's evidence, must choose between her mission and the massacre's exposure. She lets the convoy pass and transmits the Kestrel Valley files herself. Beat: climax — chaos, sacrifice, and an enemy choosing conscience over protocol.

chapters.title: After the Record Restores
chapters.summary: POV: Zephyrine. Weeks later, hearings begin; Flight 447 exists again in the public record, and Reyes testifies. Zephyrine's secret is out too — he's suspended, half-vindicated, and visits Marisol Vance's grave to finally say what happened. Beat: bittersweet resolution — justice arrived outside the law, and the price was the self he'd been guarding.
